correctness.rationale: Upper bound is sound: Perfect_1 subset limsup a-thick set at a=1/2 and HMP Lemma 3.1 gives dim<=3/2. Lower-bound headline 'a.s. dim=3/2 for continuum GFF' is NOT proved. What is machine-certified is BRW-model DP (reproduced: P1 table, tilted energies 3.14/6.70/8.62/12.37 at K=10 etc. match json). Essential GFF transfer is asserted, not proved: (i) Kahane comparison claimed to preserve exponential rate and O(1) tilted ratio up to constants uniform on Q0 from variance/increment numeric checks on k=2..5 only — no covariance-majorization matrices, no treatment of barrier indicators (non-convex) vs Kahane's convex-exponential scope; (ii) Paley-Zygmund/weak-compactness Frostman limit for two-sided tube stated without tightness/energy-lower-semicontinuity/support argument, using dyadic 2^-K scales not HMP factorial scales; (iii) Domain-Markov 0-to-1 boost ('harmonic shift absorbed by taking C larger') stated without bound: sup of harmonic extension on subdisc is unbounded Gaussian, no conditioning/quantitative absorption shown. Model-side asymptotics also overstated: F1 claims P1=c0 2^-K/2 K^-1/2(1+o(1)) but reproduced P1*2^K/2*sqrt(K)=12.92,16.24,17.72,19.22,20.41,21.31 at K=10,15,20,25,30,40 (strictly growing, effective poly exponent q~0.13-0.35, pre-asymptotic); compute_rates.py assumes K^-3/2 (corr -1.5 log2K/K) contradicting draft's K^-1/2 correction -(log2K)/2K and circular for rates.json. F2 claims raw R_j~2^j K/(K-j) (naive cap at s=1) but logged dp_verify.json gives R/2^j=1.0,0.51,0.21,0.07,0.022,0.006,0.0015,... decaying, i.e. R_j~2^{j/2} not 2^j; both raw S_1.4 (26.8->63.7) and tilted S_1.4 (9.2->13.7) still grow in K to 30-40, and s=1.49 tilted 8.6->36.8 growing, so uniform boundedness for all s<3/2 is summand-heuristic extrapolation, not uniform-cap certificate. Q-boundary fix (Q0=[1/4,1/2]^2) is honest and sound. Overall: valuable BRW ballot/tilt calculations reproduced, but continuum a.s. equality does not follow from logged certificates.

originality.rationale: TARGET route. Fused live retrieval (SerpBase Top10 + Crossref Top15 per query, OpenAlex ok with 0 hits, no partial failure) plus full-text HMP check finds no prior stating or implying one-sided O(1) uniform-envelope persistence dim 3/2 or universal thick-plus-barrier first-moment rate 3/2 for every fixed C. HMP proves dim 2-a for limsup/exact-limit sets T(a), T^C(a) via two-sided o(t) tubes E_m with radius sqrt(log(m+1)) on factorial scales s_n=1/n! plus F_{n+1} linear envelope; P(a) subset T^C. Perfect_1 (exists C with h_{2^-k}>=k ln2-C for ALL k, one-sided O(1)) is neither contained in nor implied by P(a): HMP allows o(t) dips and requires upper control, Perfect_1 allows upward spikes but forbids >O(1) dips. Aru-Papon-Powell is topological (total disconnectedness), Chen treats two-scale increments (f-steep), Rhodes-Vargas review treats liminf GMC carriers — none gives uniform-envelope dimension or barrier survival exponent. No database row covers it.

value.rationale: If proved, the statement would be independently retrievable: exact dimension 3/2 for canonical interior object (gamma0=1, fixed boundary-avoiding square, dyadic circle averages) deciding whether uniform barrier costs exponential increment vs polynomial correction — recognized frontier since Kahane/HMP/Duplantier-Sheffield/Rhodes-Vargas/Aru with downstream SLE/LQG/KPZ carrier use. Not textbook restatement, parameter substitution, or tiny gain; gamma=1 is fixed interior representative, quantification over all fixed C avoids tuning. Value holds as statement-worth, independent of current proof gap.

No one-sided O(1) uniform-envelope dim and no joint thick-plus-barrier rate 3/2 uniformly over Q.

broader_coverage.evidence: Searched dominance query for stronger theorem / broader class / larger range / census / classification / GMC-support database that could cover Perfect_1 as special case (query 3). Hits were HMP dim 2-a for all a, Chen steep points in any dimension recovering thick, 4D/high-D thick points, GMC support/exact dimensionality, BRW/ballot. Full-text comparison: HMP upper bound covers limsup supersets (used correctly for draft upper bound) but HMP lower bound is for limit set via two-sided tubes, not one-sided uniform envelope; Chen's increment sets are disjoint; GMC carriers are liminf supersets larger than O(1) envelope. No broader theorem implies uniform-envelope lower bound; barrier cost polynomial vs exponential is not decided by any broader census found.
broader_coverage.search: Query 3: Hausdorff dimension thick points GFF Hu Miller Peres steep points census classification GMC support; screened fused Top-20, fetched HMP HTML full text Sec 3.
broader_coverage.why_not_cover: Broader limsup/liminf/increment results are supersets or disjoint objects; lower bound for smaller one-sided uniform subset does not follow from lower bound for larger/different sets, and upper bound for superset does not imply lower bound.

claim_vs_prior_implication.evidence: HMP Lemmas 3.1-3.4 (fetched): Lemma 3.1 upper bounds T_{>=}^{C,s}; Lemmas 3.2-3.4 lower-bound T^C via P(a). Draft's Perfect_1 requires exists C with lower bound for all k (O(1) dips only); HMP P(a) points satisfy |B-sqrt(2a)t|=o(t) (allows -sqrt(t) dips) and require upper envelope. Neither set contains the other. Draft's tilted two-sided tube F_{C,C+} (upper C+=5) is subset of F_C, so its dim lower-bounds Perfect_1 — direction correct — but no prior source proves its dim is 3/2; HMP proof with sqrt(log k) radii and factorial scales does not give O(1) barrier with dyadic scales.
claim_vs_prior_implication.search: Compared theorem hypotheses/conclusions literally (not title similarity): HMP exact-limit vs draft uniform-envelope definitions; checked Em/Fm formulas and Lemma 3.2 inclusion.
claim_vs_prior_implication.why_not_cover: No prior result substantively implies K^{-1}log2 E[N_{K,C}]->3/2 for every fixed C with uniform barrier, nor dim Perfect_1=3/2; HMP machinery is adaptable template but adaptation (Bessel/ballot + upper truncation + Kahane transfer) is the claimed novelty, not a corollary/recomputation.

Fused results returned only HMP, expository term papers, high-D thick points, steep points; no 'uniformly thick perfect envelope dim 3/2' statement found.

equivalent_formulations.why_not_cover: HMP 'perfect thick points' are two-sided o(t) tubes for limsup supersets, terminologically overlapping but mathematically distinct from draft's one-sided O(1)-for-all-k Perfect_1; no dual/complement/matrix encoding was found that restates the uniform-envelope claim.

exact_database_or_table.evidence: No specialist table, repository, thesis, or author page lists Perfect_1 dimension or thick-plus-barrier survival rate. Search included specialist-database directions; only generic reviews and HMP/Cipriani slides found. Local artifacts (dp_verify.json, tilted_certificate.json, rates.json) are new computations, not reprints: rates.json analytic K^-3/2 table is inconsistent with DP K^-1/2 fit, confirming not copied from prior table.
exact_database_or_table.search: Database/table direction in queries 1-3 plus screening for rows/tables covering exact parameter (gamma=1, Q, every fixed C, rate 3/2).
exact_database_or_table.why_not_cover: Exact parameter/object does not appear in any official database or table; finding is not a recomputation/repackaging of a tabulated value.

residual_risks: OpenAlex returned 0 hits per query (status ok, not a failure); coverage relies on SerpBase+Crossref+fused full-text HMP check — recorded, does not establish priority.
Continuum transfer gap is structural (Kahane for barrier indicators, Frostman limit, Markov boost), not closable by re-running DP at larger K.
Finite-K DP cannot by itself settle K^-1/2 vs K^-3/2 polynomial or uniform-in-K energy boundedness; larger-K/finer-dx runs would reduce discretization risk but not fix transfer.
